definitions.standard: A large, muscular sheet that forms the floor of the chest cavity and helps in breathing.
definitions.simple: A strong muscle below your lungs that pulls down to suck air in, and pushes up to force air out.
definitions.scientific: A dome-shaped, muscular partition separating the thorax from the abdomen in mammals. It plays a major role in breathing, as its contraction increases the volume of the thorax and so inflates the lungs.

examples: Hiccups are caused by spasms of the diaphragm
real_world_applications: Singers train their diaphragm to hold long notes

advanced_data.history: Ancient Greeks thought the diaphragm was the seat of the mind or emotions.

common_misconceptions: Lungs suck in air on their own. (False, the lungs have no muscles! The diaphragm does the pulling).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Compare the diaphragm to the handle of a bicycle pump or a syringe.
